detail.reason: Lower-slope streambank ~0.5 mi from trailhead; it is a low point in a draw, not high ground — contradicts the single dominant signature.
Enclosed creek crossing among trees and switchbacks; no broad outward vista.
Streambank rocks and roots form small natural niches, but these are minor, not a defining stone recess.
Cache could rest against streambank rocks/roots at/above ground; no digging needed.
Some streambank rocks present, but the operative landmark here is the water/crossing, not a sittable boulder or outcrop.

Water is definitively present, but this is a CROSSING — the trail crosses the creek, conflicting with 'never crossed / stay on dry bank'. Bank could host the spot but the crossing nature works against it.
Wooded SE slope, but no notable adjacent clearing/meadow/field edge described.
On the established Grindstone Trail, easy-moderate walk, right at a trail junction; non-dangerous footing.
~0.5 mi from parking, well under 3 mi from road, no climbing or hazard.
Lower-slope crossing is unremarkable but is also a busy junction where hikers turn; not especially secluded.
No paired crags or notch framing the spot; it is a drainage crossing.
Wooded streambank with roots, but no specific prominent oak/pine marker called out.
SE side of park, but as a creek crossing in a draw it has no defined cardinal view orientation.
No distinctive rounded/domed/egg stone described at the crossing.
Wet, slippery streambank plausibly mossy, but not explicitly a moss-against-stone color marker.
Granitic-gneiss bedrock generally, but no quartz/sparkle cue noted at this streambank specifically.
No bedding/columnar/blocky stone feature described here.
No reddish/iron-stained or golden stone cue at the crossing.
No pale/white standout stone marker described.

No inscription/seam noted; a natural streambank lacks a fixed up-close confirming mark.
